items.title: Instruction boxes obscure fighter footwork
items.what: In screenshots 3, 4, 9, 10, and 11, the semi-transparent 'STANCE' and 'TECHNIQUE' text boxes (listing inputs like 'step', 'jump', 'crouch') are positioned directly above the analog sticks. This places them directly over the fighters' feet and lower legs.
items.why: In a karate game, footwork, stance, and leg positioning are critical mechanics for spacing and defense. Obscuring the feet makes it difficult for the player to judge distance and see if a crouch or jump is visually registering.
items.how: Fade these instruction boxes out after 5 seconds of inactivity, or move them to the top of the screen (below the score bar), or reduce their opacity/size significantly so they don't block the action.

items.title: Game renders in landscape orientation
items.what: Screenshot 12 shows the game running in a landscape aspect ratio. The fighters are tiny in the center, the background is stretched wide, and the analog sticks are spaced far apart at the bottom.
items.why: The design baseline is a portrait phone (390x844). Running in landscape breaks the UI layout, makes the fighters too small to see details, and likely breaks the touch controls.
items.how: Lock the browser/game orientation to portrait mode in the WebGPU/Three.js initialization code.

items.title: Impact text obscures the hit
items.what: In screenshot 9 ('IP PON' screen), the large 'IP PON' text and the move name 'SPINNING BACK KICK' are centered on the screen. This stack of text overlaps the fighters, obscuring the moment of impact.
items.why: The player needs to see the hit connect to feel the impact. Blocking the view of the fighters during a 'hit stop' moment reduces the visual feedback of the successful move.
items.how: Move the 'IP PON' text higher up (near the top HUD) or make the text semi-transparent so the action remains visible behind it.

items.title: Techniques menu is too dense to read
items.what: In screenshot 5, the 'TECHNIQUES' menu lists moves in a dense, long list. The icons (small circles with arrows) and the text are small and cramped.
items.why: On a mobile screen, this density makes it hard to quickly scan for a specific move or understand the input combination (e.g., 'Right Stick Forward' + 'Up').
items.how: Increase the font size and icon size. Consider grouping moves by direction (Forward, Back, Up, Down) in a grid or card layout instead of a single long list.

items.title: Score uses cluttered fraction notation
items.what: In screenshot 7 ('HASANABI WINS'), the score is displayed as '2 1/2'.
items.why: The fraction '1/2' is visually cluttered and takes up more horizontal space than necessary, making the score look messy compared to a clean decimal.
items.how: Use decimal notation '2.5' for a cleaner, more modern UI look.
